name: structseq_repr
note: review: structseqRepr computes prealloc = strlen(tp_name) + 1 + Py_SIZE * 5 + 1 (:281-282) in unbounded Int and its writer (UnicodeObj/ObjectWriter.lean) cannot fail to allocate, so ReprShape's \"for every object\" is false on CPython for Py_SIZE around 2^35 and above, which copy.replace reaches after time.struct_time.n_sequence_fields = 2**40: PyUnicodeWriter_Create (Objects/unicode_writer.c:105-132) raises MemoryError (past 2^61 the Py_ssize_t product overflows to a negative length and ValueError) where the theorem predicts the SystemError at the tp_members sentinel; the item __repr__ failure path is mirrored, and typeobj-structseq-repr-labels is a well-founded refutation (gh-154387 duplicate).

name: structseq_reduce
note: review: ReduceInBoundsHonest assumes u <= v (HonestLayout), which its registry statement presents as \"the size attributes PyStructSequence_NewType stored\", but NewType does not enforce it and Doc/c-api/tuple.rst does not state it (only the source comment at :23-24 does): fields [x, unnamed, unnamed] with n_in_sequence = 1 build a type whose __reduce__ reads tp_members[-1] at :369, the interesting case the hypothesis removes; the theorem holds for a reduceC that always raises, and the only functional property, ReduceRoundTrip, runs on the StructSeq.lean structseqReduce, which has none of the failure paths (n_unnamed_fields read, NULL items, member-name decoding).

name: structseq_replace
note: review: Both models compare keyword names with pure equality (popKw in StructSeqC.lean, popName in StructSeq.lean), but PyDict_PopString (Objects/dictobject.c:3326-3339) compares an exact str with the kwargs keys, and a str-subclass keyword (copy.replace(t, **{S('tm_year'): 1}), S defining __hash__ = str.__hash__ and an __eq__ that raises) runs Python code that can raise, where ReplaceSpec claims success; ReplaceSpec is also over the abstract model without the size reads, the allocation or the decode failure, and the C mirror's ReplaceInBoundsHonest would hold for a replaceC that always raised.

name: PyStructSequence_NewType
